children: Zip's bull at Jefferies says the Australian payments provider looks reasonably priced considering its exposure to the growing U.S. buy-now-pay-later sector. Analyst Evan Karatzas keeps a buy rating on the stock after Zip's September-quarter results showed it was among the companies gaining market share in the period. Zip has been profitably penetrating the U.S. installment-payments market and should continue to do so, he says. Jefferies raises its target price on the ASX-listed stock to 12.80 Australian dollars, from A$2.90, which also accounts for a recent 5-for-1 consolidation. Shares are up 6.4% at A$8.31. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
